findings.text: The cycle helper advances an index by one position within a configured length, wrapping to the start when deadlock mode is requested and otherwise reporting absence with a negative value at the end, while emitting a diagnostic line that differs depending on whether a successor exists.

The sleepable dependency self test is gated by a control value, decodes its thousands digit as deadlock request, middle digits as test selector and units digit as cycle length, warns and aborts to usage output on malformed deadlock or nonpositive length, otherwise dispatches to one of four exercises or falls through to usage output when the selector is unrecognized or support is unavailable.

The pure sleepable exercise iterates over the cycle, acquires a read side critical section on the current instance, optionally waits for a grace period of the successor instance, then releases the current instance with its acquisition cookie, thereby creating ordered nesting between read holdings and waits.

The mixed exercises pair each sleepable read section with same position mutual exclusion or reader writer semaphore operations in one direction and pair same position exclusive ownership with successor grace period waits in the opposite direction, establishing two lock orderings per cycle position for dependency checking.

When trace support is compiled in, the mixed chain uses a trace read side critical section at position zero and sleepable read sections elsewhere, waiting on sleepable successors except for the final position which waits on the trace grace period, otherwise the selector produces usage output.

The torture initialization selects a test operations descriptor by matching a configured type name, reports valid names and fails with invalid argument status when no match exists, and otherwise proceeds through parameter adjustment, state reset and worker creation.

Initialization follows an ordered startup of freelist setup, counter reset, fake writers, readers, writer, up down threads, offload toggles, statistics, shuffling, stutter, quiescent forcing, boosting, shutdown, online offline, stall, forward progress, barrier and exit paths, with any failure transferring to a common unwind that finalizes setup, cleans up and optionally powers off.

A stall only request suppresses most activity toggles, nonnegative fake writer and reader counts are used directly while negative values derive a positive count from online processor count with a floor of one, and several interval and duration controls are clamped to nonnegative or minimum values before use.

Each reference scale reader record holds a thread handle, an integer start flag, a wait queue for coordination, and a sixty four bit measurement of last iteration duration, with separate global main thread handle, main wait queue and dynamically sized reader record array.

A reference scale operations descriptor provides optional initialization and cleanup hooks, a tight read section hook, a read section with delays hook, a flag controlling interrupt handling, and a name string used for selection and reporting, with a global current pointer selecting the active descriptor.

All read and delay variants loop over a supplied iteration count inclusive of zero, with delay variants inserting microsecond and nanosecond pauses inside the protected region through a shared helper that skips each pause type when its argument is zero.

Sleepable reference scale tests share a global control pointer defaulting to the normal instance, with fast and fast up down initializers redirecting it to their respective instances, and each variant pairs its own fast or normal acquisition and release primitives using either an integer cookie or a per processor counter handle.

The tasks variant performs no protection and only loops or delays, the trace variant brackets iterations with trace read side acquisition and release, and baseline variants replace read side primitives with global atomic increment decrement pairs or per processor increment decrement pairs.

The default reference scale type name is rcu and diagnostic output uses a fixed marker identifying reference scale messages, with quiet and verbose reporting paths controlled by verbosity and batching controls.
Single element deadlock cycles for pure sleepable and mixed trace exercises intentionally risk a hang and announce that expectation, since each iteration waits on the instance it currently holds.

Failed initialization always runs cleanup after finalizing setup, and when a shutdown interval is configured the failure path additionally warns about module expectations and requests power off, making startup failures potentially destructive.
Experiment progress uses separate atomic counters for expected readers, initialization, start, warmup and cooldown phases plus an integer experiment index, isolating lifecycle stages.

Availability of tasks and trace descriptors is controlled by compile time selection, with the corresponding table entry expanding either to a descriptor pointer or to nothing, so unsupported builds silently omit those variants.
